source: Round-24 V2 builder hand-test on T-02 (feature flag). First multi-task organic harness run; second non-T-01 dispatch. Validates that the V2 builder picks up data-driven precedent patterns (single union + single defaults map) rather than creating a new file per the plan's incorrect assumption.

actual_baseline.notes: Subagent grep'd for `vetsEnabled` and discovered the data-driven pattern: single FeatureFlag union member + single defaults map entry; remoteConfigService derives keys from Object.keys(defaultFeatureFlags) so no third edit is needed there. Mirror was minimal (2 functional lines). 3 test fixture files needed `incidentsEnabled: false` added to keep tsc -b green after widening the union — flagged in notes as mechanical type-driven edits, not behavior changes. The subagent correctly judged this as in-scope rather than escalating as a SPEC_GAP — a reasonable reading: §D2 file map doesn't list test files, but type-soundness of test fixtures is a direct consequence of the union edit.

notes: Validates: (a) V2 builder picks up implicit precedent patterns from grep, not just the literal §D2 file list; (b) builder makes scope-judgment calls about type-driven mechanical edits without escalating; (c) the harness pattern works on a non-T-01 task. The plan's 'Files expected to change' incorrectly listed `src/featureFlags/incidentsFlag.ts` as a new file — the subagent correctly disregarded the plan and mirrored the actual precedent. Empirical confirmation that subagent reasoning trumps plan-author guesses about file structure.
